newsitem.title: CHINA: China blast kills 12, police hunt for saboteurs.
newsitem.headline: China blast kills 12, police hunt for saboteurs.

text.p: Chinese police are hunting for saboteurs who blew up an explosives warehouse in southeast China last month, killing 12 construction workers living next door, a local official said on Thursday.

A warehouse illegally storing explosives in Kangmei town in Fujian province blew up on February 1, killing 12 migrant workers who were living in an adjacent building, said an official with the town government.
Authorities suspected local residents were behind the blast to take revenge on the workers, who had been brought in from other parts of China to lay a new road, he said.

"We think the motive for the explosion was that local people were unhappy with the workers," he said, adding he did not know if residents were angry at the workers themselves or were upset with the road project for taking up farmland.
Police had not found those responsible for setting off the explosion but had arrested three owners of the warehouse for storing the explosives illegally, he said.
Chinese media did not report the blast, but newspapers often carry reports of bombings carried out by disgruntled workers or jilted lovers.
Beijing was rocked last week when a bomb blast ripped through a public bus. Sources said the explosion killed at least two people and injured dozens, but China says no one was killed.

Authorities have not given a motive for the Beijing attack. But police say it was unrelated to three bomb attacks last month on buses in Urumqi, capital of the restive northwestern region of Xinjiang, in which nine people died and 74 were wounded.
